original.description: The Advancing Sectoral Emission Monitoring is a Fixed Call for Proposal for RD projects advancing the detection and quantificationof greenhouse gas (CH4, CO2 or other species with a radiative forcing effect) and air pollutants emissions for specific sectors. Targeted sectors are defined as in international and European policies (IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories, EU-ETS, CBAM, main sectors contributing to global methane emissions, Industrial Emissions Portal Regulation, ...). The activity will alsovelop complementary sector-specific information such as activity data to produce EO-based policy-relevant information. The activityforesees the direct involvement of relevant stakeholders in the project. This Call for Proposal will lead to up to four contracts, with a maximum value of 800 kEuros and an implementation over a 2-year period.

original.description: The overall goal of ARTES 4.0 Business Applications can be summarised as the development of pre-operational services - possibly in partnership - for a wide range of users through the combination of different systems. Business Applications activities aim at: i) collecting user feedback for better tuning of the applications and the operation of all elements involved, ii) developing commercial sustainable space based applications by linking user needs to corresponding solutions incorporating space assets requesting only limited technology adaptations, iii) demonstrating to users and stakeholders that the proposed solutions work in their operational environment and are compatible with their operational practices, iv) utilising at least one space asset (such as Satellite Communications, Earth Observation, Satellite Navigation, Human Spaceflight, or any other space asset, service or technology), leading to a better exploitation of existing space capacity and know-how together with a better understanding of how they should evolve to respond to user needs. ARTES 4.0 Business Applications operates via a 'Call for Proposals' which is always open. Partners respond with proposals as they find it opportune. The activities proposed in response to this 'Call for Proposals' must be relevant to above mentioned ARTES 4.0 Business Applications objectives. Although not a competitive tender action, this Call for Proposals' is published on esa-star Publication in order to achieve a higher degree of visibility. The closing date that is mentioned upon issue of the Call for Proposals is established solely for technical reasons connected with the esa-star Publication system and can be disregarded.

original.description: The ACCESS (Accelerating Commercialisation and Competitiveness of the European Space Sector) programme helps companies develop innovative commercial products and services that strengthen European competitiveness in both space and non-space markets. It fosters a diverse and dynamic space ecosystem, ensuring that the benefits of commercialisation reach all Participating States.Business Applications and Space Solutions (BASS) is the element of ACCESS programme specifically designed to accelerate the transformation of innovative ideas into market-ready space-based services and applications that deliver measurable socio-economic impact.BASS offers to companies and academia derisking tools to mitigate technical and commercial risks, shortening the path from concept to market. With a strong user-driven focus, BASS creates the conditions for commercial success and positions space as a driver of innovation, competitiveness, and lasting value for society.To deliver these outcomes, BASS offers a comprehensive support package which includes zero-equity funding, tailored business and technical expertise, project management guidance, ESA branding, and access to commercialisation networks. This ecosystem connects companies with customers, investors, and partners, enabling them to overcome market barriers whilesecuring sustainable growth through private investment and demand-driven adoption.BASS support is tailored to every stage of developmentfrom assessing the viability of new space-based applications, to designing, implementing, and piloting space-based solutions and supporting their expansion into new markets.

original.description: Under NAVISP Element 3, the Agency issues this Call for Proposals for the development of initiatives in the Position, Navigation and Timing domain. Element 3 is focused on participating States' priorities and aims at supporting their national navigation activities along the whole value chain. Element 3 configures as an ad-hoc support element, which is envisaged per country and possibly per domain, for the development and promotion of products, applications and services based on GNSS and more widely on PNT systems. Following participating states request, ESA may provide technical assistance in various areas. Element 3 configures as an opportunity for the participating States delegations to animate and coordinate discussions with national entities and to set up the processes to identify and federate institutional demands. This will foster cooperation as well as possible national partnerships with a wide diversity of actors, enlarging the national space community (agency, industries, universities, and research centres) and strengthening its relationships with authorities, organisations, institutions, industries, and research actors from non-space sectors. Industry and research institutes of Participant States are encouraged to contact the NAVISP Element 3 team to discuss the development of activities of national relevance and matching institutional interests. Details on the tendering process and preparing the Full Proposal are provided in the Standard Call for Proposals.

original.description: The activities in GSTP Element 2 "Make" aim to strengthen worldwide competitiveness in the near term in existing markets, establish strategic capabilities which will result in stronger competitiveness in the medium term on existing or new markets, and to support the implementation of National priorities. GSTP Element 2 "Make" aims to support design, development, and demonstration activities. Products and technologies are defined to be any hardware, software, or applications within the scope set out in section 3 below. Key characteristics of this Element are:  The role of industry in defining and proposing projects oriented to commercial or institutional opportunities in all areas of satellite applications except satellite telecommunication (not covered by GSTP);  The outcome of an activity will eventually become a product ready for exploitation.  The sharing of funding by ESA and industry. Activities submitted in the frame of GSTP Element 2 Make" may be related to the improvement or development of satellite subsystems or equipment (including EGSE), space transportation subsystems or equipment up to engineering model or qualification model, and the improvement or development of ground / user system and equipment up to prototypes and commercialized products. Activities should address any the following technology themes: Earth observation, science, exploration, human spaceflight, space transportation, satellite navigation or generic technologies.

original.description: Under NAVISP Element 2, the Agency issues this permanently open Standard Call for Proposals without procurement, using Cooperative Agreements as contractual instrument.This Standard Call for Proposals without procurement aims to enhance Participant States' industrial competitiveness in the evolving Positioning, Navigation, and Timing (PNT) sector. Industry is invited to submit proposals to develop innovative and competitive PNT-related products. The Agency accepts proposals from both space and non-space companies, including large companies, mid-caps, small enterprises, and start-ups. Proposed products may address the satellite space segment, ground infrastructure, and user segment, including applications and services. Industry and research institutes of Participant States are encouraged to contact the NAVISP Element 2 team to discuss the development of pre-operational products aligned with their strategiesand plans. Details on the tendering process and how to prepare the Full Proposal are provided in the Standard Call for Proposals without procurement documentation.

original.description: The objective of this activity is to co-fund PhD projects focusing on Exploration Science relevant topics.Exploration Science PhDs will target high-priority, exploration-driven science topics, whilealso advancing exploration-enabled research directly linked toongoing missions and projects of the European Space Agency. Building on the existing ESA OSIP co-sponsored Research programme, these positions will be recruited through a dedicated call and alignedwith Explore2040 priorities with a primary focus on science thematics such as local resources, environments  effects, crew health and performance, and habitation and with a secondary focus on enabled science linked to key missions and projects (e.g. ExoMars or ACES).By embedding these PhDs within leading academic institutions, ESA fosters a distributed network of high-potential early-career scientists working on mission-relevant challenges.This strengthens ties with academia, accelerates the maturation of key scientific domains, and ensures a sustained pipeline of expertise closely aligned with Explore2040 objectives.
